## Q1
Which of the following statement(s) do NOT hold true with respect to Vocational Education as per NEP-2020?<br>
A. B.Voc degrees introduced in 2013 will be discontinued.<br>
B. Lok Vidya courses will replace existing vocational courses.<br>
C. Focus areas for vocational education will be chosen on skills gap analysis without mapping local opportunities.<br>
D. National Committee for Integration of Vocational Education will be constituted.<br>
E. Vocational education will be integrated into all schools and higher education institutions in a phased manner over the next decade. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

## Q1 - Options
(A) A, B and C only
(B) B, C and D only
(C) C, D and E only
(D) A, C and D only

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q44

NEP 2020 does not say B.Voc will be discontinued, does not make Lok Vidya a replacement for all vocational courses, and requires local opportunities to be mapped. Thus A, B and C do not hold true.

## Q4
Which of the following explain the concept of values?

A. Values are beliefs tied inextricably to human emotion and behaviour.<br>
B. Values refer to desirable goals people strive to attain.<br>
C. Values are conflict-free.<br>
D. Values are ordered by importance relative to one another.<br>
E. Values are utilized primarily to effect change in a person’s knowledge.

Choose the correct answer.

## Q4 - Options
(A) A, B and C only
(B) A, B and D only
(C) B, C and D only
(D) C, D and E only

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2020 (11 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q42

Values are enduring beliefs linked to emotion and behaviour, express desirable goals, and are arranged in a personal hierarchy of importance. They may conflict, and they are not confined to changing knowledge, so A, B and D is correct.

## Q6

Statement I: Equality of educational opportunities is a pre-condition for achieving equity in education.<br>
Statement II: Equity in education can be achieved without equality of educational opportunities.

Choose the correct answer.

## Q6 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2020 (11 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q44

Equal access to educational opportunities is a necessary foundation for equitable educational outcomes. Statement II denies that foundation, so Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

## Q7
What are the advantages of the Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) introduced by the UGC for higher education institutions?

A. Focuses on student-centric education<br>
B. Allows students to choose interdisciplinary and intra-disciplinary courses<br>
C. Makes education at par with global standards<br>
D. Makes it easy to estimate student performance in terms of marks<br>
E. Offers flexibility for students to undertake studies at different times and institutions

Choose the correct answer.

## Q7 - Options
(A) A, B, C and D only
(B) B, C, D and E only
(C) A, B, C and E only
(D) C, D, E and A only

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2020 (11 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q45

CBCS is student-centred, permits course choice across disciplines, supports comparability with broader credit systems, and offers mobility and flexibility. It is not principally designed merely to estimate performance in terms of marks, so A, B, C and E is correct.

## Q8
The major barriers for access to higher education in India are :

(a) more opportunities of employment for less educated<br>
(b) government policies<br>
(c) language of instruction<br>
(d) economic status<br>
(e) competition from foreign universities<br>
(f) gender discrimination in society

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q8 - Options
(A) (a), (b) and (c)
(B) (b). (c) and (e)
(C) (c). (d) and (f)
(D) (d), (e) and (f)

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q42

Linguistic medium, household economic constraints, and societal gender inequities are the most pronounced structural barriers hindering equitable access to higher education in India.

- **(a) More opportunities of employment for less educated** — incorrect. Structural youth unemployment is high among less educated individuals.
- **(b) Government policies** — affirmative action, scholarships, and fee waivers aim to expand access rather than act as primary systemic barriers.
- **(c) Language of instruction** — English dominance creates severe hurdles for students transitioning from vernacular-medium regional schools.
- **(d) Economic status** — high tuition, accommodation costs, and opportunity costs severely restrict low-income family enrollment.
- **(e) Competition from foreign universities** — foreign universities enroll a tiny fraction of elite students and do not limit domestic higher education access.
- **(f) Gender discrimination in society** — patriarchal attitudes and early marriage pressures disproportionately suppress female higher education participation.

Selecting the structural barriers yields statements (c), (d), and (f).

## Q9
According to GATS (General Agreement on Trade and Services), higher education should be a commodity in the

## Q9 - Options
(A) domestic public sector
(B) domestic private sector
(C) non-trading sector
(D) global marketplace

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q43

The World Trade Organization's General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) classifies higher education as a commercially tradable service within the global marketplace.

- Under GATS framework, educational services are treated as economic commodities open to international cross-border trade, commercial presence, and global investment across member nations.
- **A. Domestic public sector** — traditional state-funded education model that GATS seeks to open to international private trade.
- **B. Domestic private sector** — focuses solely on national private providers rather than the global trade regimes established under WTO.
- **C. Non-trading sector** — GATS specifically removes higher education from non-trading exemptions by treating it as commercial service.
- **D. Global marketplace** — correct. GATS conceptualizes education as an internationally marketable commodity traded across borders.

## Q10
Which of the following statements is true in the Indian context?

## Q10 - Options
(A) Autonomous colleges can grant degrees independent of universities
(B) Autonomous colleges can grant only bachelor's degree independent of universities
(C) Except doctoral degrees, all other degrees and diplomas can be granted by autonomous colleges
(D) Whatever may be the degree or diploma, autonomous colleges can grant them under their own name but under the seal of an affiliated university

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q44

Under UGC guidelines on autonomous colleges, autonomy grants academic and administrative freedom over curriculum and examinations, but degree-awarding power remains vested in the affiliating parent university.

- **A, B, C** are incorrect because autonomous colleges in India do not hold university status and cannot award independent academic degrees on their own authority.
- **D. Whatever may be the degree or diploma, autonomous colleges can grant them under their own name but under the seal of an affiliated university** — correct. The diploma or degree bears the college's name, but must be issued under the formal seal, authority, and accreditation of the affiliating university.

## Q11
Rashtriya Uchhatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) aims to achieve the following in Higher Education System:

(a) Equity<br>
(b) Access<br>
(c) 50% GER<br>
(d) Excellence

Choose the correct option from those given below:

## Q11 - Options
(A) (a), (b) and (c)
(B) (a), (c) and (d)
(C) (a), (b) and (d)
(D) (b), (c) and (d)

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q45

Rashtriya Uchhatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) is built upon three foundational strategic pillars: Access, Equity, and Excellence in state higher education institutions.

- **(a) Equity** — target pillar providing targeted funding to socially disadvantaged groups, women, and unserved educationally backward districts.
- **(b) Access** — target pillar aimed at expanding institutional capacity, infrastructure, and geographical reach.
- **(c) 50% GER** — incorrect target. RUSA 1.0 targeted raising the gross enrolment ratio to 30% by 2020 (50% GER by 2035 was later introduced by NEP 2020).
- **(d) Excellence** — target pillar enhancing academic faculty quality, accreditation, governance, and research infrastructure.

Combining the three foundational pillars yields statements (a), (b), and (d).

## Q12
In post independence India, which one of the following Committee/Commission’s report deals with all levels of education in India?

## Q12 - Options
(A) Sargeant Commission
(B) Hartog Committee
(C) Kothari Commission
(D) Radhakrishnan Commission

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q40

The Kothari Commission (Education Commission, 1964–66), chaired by Daulat Singh Kothari, was explicitly mandated to formulate a comprehensive national policy covering all stages of education.

- **A. Sargeant Commission** — the 1944 Post-War Educational Development memorandum was formulated prior to independence.
- **B. Hartog Committee** — established in 1929 to evaluate educational growth, also preceding independence.
- **C. Kothari Commission** — correct. Appointed in 1964, its landmark report Education and National Development provided recommendations spanning primary, secondary, vocational, and higher education.
- **D. Radhakrishnan Commission** — the University Education Commission (1948–49) focused specifically on post-independence university education.

## Q13
Which one of the following instructional designs is not a part of SWAYAM launched by Government of India?

## Q13 - Options
(A) E-tutorial
(B) E-Content
(C) Physical interaction
(D) Discussion Forum

## Q13 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q43

The SWAYAM online educational platform is structured around a four-quadrant instructional framework developed specifically for digital remote learning.

The four quadrants of SWAYAM are:

1. e-Tutorial — recorded video lectures and audio demonstrations
2. e-Content — digital reading materials, downloadable texts, and case studies
3. Assessment — self-assessment quizzes, tests, and assignments
4. Discussion forum — an interactive online space for clearing doubts

As a fully web-based MOOC ecosystem, SWAYAM delivers its coursework entirely online and does not include mandatory in-person physical interaction.

## Q14

## Q14 - Options

(B) AIU
(C) NUEPA
(D) ICSSR

## Q14 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q45

The Inter-University Board was established in 1925 in Shimla to foster mutual cooperation, coordinate academic activities, and facilitate credit recognition across Indian universities.

- **A. UGC** — the University Grants Commission was established as a statutory body in 1956 to coordinate, determine, and maintain standards of university education.

## Q15
The Education Commission of India that first took serious note of the problem of Brain Drain was

## Q15 - Options
(A) The Education Commission of India
(B) The University Education Commission
(C) The Calcutta University Commission
(D) The Sargeant Commission

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2019 (24 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q48

The Education Commission of India (1964–66), headed by D. S. Kothari, was the first official statutory commission in India to formally investigate and sound the alarm on the loss of highly trained scientific talent abroad.

In its comprehensive report, the Commission devoted specific attention to the emigration of doctors, scientists, engineers, and scholars to developed nations, which it termed Brain Drain, urging the government to establish research infrastructure and competitive conditions to retain Indian intellectuals.

- **A. The Education Commission of India** — correct. The official title of the Kothari Commission (1964–66).
- **B. The University Education Commission** — headed by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1948–49), focused on foundational university development.
- **C. The Calcutta University Commission** — the Sadler Commission (1917–19), examined university and secondary schooling in Bengal during colonial rule.
- **D. The Sargeant Commission** — the 1944 pre-independence scheme for post-war educational reconstruction.

## Q17
University and University-level institutions are categorized into:

a. Central Universities b. State Universities c. Private Universities d. Deemed-to-be Universities e. Institutions of Higher Learning f. Civil Sector Institutions

Choose the correct combination of options:

## Q17 - Options
(A) (b), (d), (e) and (f)
(B) (a), (c), (e) and (f)
(C) (a), (b), (c) and (d)
(D) (c), (d), (e) and (f)

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q42

Under the University Grants Commission Act of 1956, higher educational institutions empowered to award degrees are formally categorized into four statutory types:

- **a. Central Universities** — established by an Act of Parliament.
- **b. State Universities** — established by an Act of a State Legislature.
- **c. Private Universities** — established by State or Central legislative acts under UGC Regulations.
- **d. Deemed-to-be Universities** — declared under Section 3 of the UGC Act on UGC recommendation.

Institutions of Higher Learning (e) and Civil Sector Institutions (f) are descriptive classifications, not formal statutory university categories. Hence, (a), (b), (c), and (d) is correct.
